items.caption: In this oracle-script style redraw, a smaller looped figure sits above a larger branching figure. The upper figure has a rounded outline open at the lower left; the lower figure has a long crosswise stroke, a descending central form, and diagonal branches. This is one reported early layout of 好, but its shapes do not settle the components’ identity or the character’s original motivation.
items.alt: Black redraw: a small looped form above a larger branching form, whose diagonal branches descend from a central junction.
items.selection_reason: The upper and lower figures differ in scale and shape, making this redraw useful for discussing the proposed 女-plus-子 analysis while keeping the original motivation unresolved.
items.period: Shang oracle-script style; modern redraw, not a dated artifact specimen

items.caption: In this bronze-script style redraw, a tall upright figure with a crosswise arm and two enclosed upper spaces stands to the left of a rounded figure with a large interior opening and a long descending tail. It shows a different arrangement of a reported 好 form, not a chronological stage after the other redraw.
items.alt: Black redraw: a tall left figure with a crosswise arm, enclosed upper spaces and a long stem; a rounded figure with an interior opening and descending tail stands to its right.
items.selection_reason: Its side-by-side arrangement helps illustrate reported variation in the placement of 女 and 子; the redraw does not establish a specimen date or graphic sequence.
items.period: Bronze-script style; no specific specimen date established

limitations.text: 好’s original motivation remains unresolved. Proposed explanations include mother–child affection, a woman’s beauty, and affection between a man and a woman; cited early uses do not directly attest the mother–child interpretation.
These are modern redrawings labeled by script tradition, not photographs of dated inscriptions. Their labels do not establish a specimen date or a chronological sequence between the forms.
